title: Toronto cop stabbing reminiscent of 2009 attack on Barrie officers
article: The stabbing that sent a Toronto police officer to hospital with a serious neck wound is reminiscent of a similar case that happened in Barrie nearly three years ago where two officers were knifed in the neck.
The Barrie police officers, who were stabbed during an attempted arrest in 2009, were honoured by Canada's Governor General David Johnson for their bravery at a February ceremony.
Constables Clayton Speers and David Edgar were responding to a call outside a busy mall on Bayfield Street near Highway 400 on July 5, 2009.

Police allege Donald Melton, 48, lunged at the officers, stabbing them both in the neck. Melton then ran from the officers, police said, and toward the mall, still waving his knife. He refused to respond to requests to drop his weapon.
Edgar, bleeding profusely, pursued Melton and fatally shot him.
Both men underwent surgery and have since returned to active duty.
Johnson presented Edgar and Speers with the Star of Courage, which "recognizes acts of conspicuous courage in circumstances of great peril."
The officers also received Ontario's medal for police bravery.
Edgar spoke to CityNews Monday and while he wouldn't comment on Monday incident directly, he said all officers "are praying for a quick recovery.

"I'm wishing the officer and his family all the best and a positive outcome...Devastating incidents such as this prove as a reminder to all of us that it is our pleasure and duty to serve and protect all the members of our community. These duties, at times, come with such risks."
